_comment: Every threshold the cockpit scores against. Nothing in src/scoring/ may
hard-code a number that belongs here.
Scores are 0-5 and are built by ADDING named components, each worth at
most 1. A component with no data contributes 0 and says so — a missing
feed must never read as a benign reading, and must never invent a signal.

meltup._comment: Section 6. Six-month return is the spine; acceleration matters more than level.

bust._comment: Section 7. Five categories, each contributing at most 1.

_comment: Section 8. Stage 0-5. Rate-of-change matters as much as level: a move
from 2.7% to 3.7% can be more informative than a static 4%.
NOTE: FRED licenses the ICE BofA tier indices (CCC/BB/IG) on a rolling
~3-year window, so the tiered ladder cannot see 2008 or 2020. Broad HY
reaches further back. The UI states this.

rates._comment: Section 11. Both directions: rising rates as trigger, collapsing rates as bust confirmation.

liquidity._comment: Section 12. Distinguish routine balance-sheet drift from emergency expansion.

commodities._comment: Section 13. Supercycle confirmation needs several signals, not one new high.

_comment: Section 4. A phase must not flip on one day's move. `persistDays` is the
number of consecutive sessions a candidate phase must hold before it is
adopted — the same hysteresis the Barometer uses on its regimes.
V2. The AI Capital Stress Score: five components, each worth at most 1.
THESE NUMBERS MUST BE FALSIFIABLE. The score is not built to confirm
that an AI capital bubble exists — it is built so that the Noble/Chanos
thesis can be shown to be WRONG by the same data that could show it to
be right. So every component has a `contradicts` level as well as a
stress level, and a company comfortably inside the contradicting level
is reported as evidence against the thesis rather than as silence.
Levels are fractions unless named otherwise: 0.35 means 35%.

intensity._comment: Capex as a share of revenue, and how fast it is growing relative to revenue. A build-out growing far faster than the revenue it serves is the precondition for the thesis, not proof of it.

funding._comment: Capex against the operating cash flow available to pay for it. Above 1 the programme is larger than the cash the business generates and is being financed from somewhere else.

_comment: The core of the thesis. Incremental operating income per additional
dollar of capital. A falling or thin incremental return while spending
accelerates is the claim; a healthy one is the refutation.
Benchmarked against a mid-teens cost of capital rather than zero:
capital earning 4% is destroying value even though 4% is positive.

financing._comment: Whether the build-out is shifting from surplus cash onto borrowed money. This is the component that connects the capital cycle to credit at all.

_comment: Supplier against buyers. Nvidia's revenue is partly the mirror image
of hyperscaler capex, so the two growing together is the normal state
of a capital cycle. The signal is DIVERGENCE: the supplier still
booking growth while the buyers' spending decelerates is the classic
shape of a cycle turning, and is what would show up first.

status._comment: The one-line AI CAPITAL status under Market Setup. Score bands, 0-5.

_comment: V2 section 10. The chain AI CAPITAL -> AI CREDIT -> CCC -> BB/B -> HY -> IG,
each node GREEN / AMBER / RED / UNKNOWN.
THE POINT OF THIS PANEL is to stop an elevated capital-cycle score
from being read as a credit event. Deteriorating capital economics
at six companies is not transmission; transmission is those
economics showing up in what lenders charge. So the credit nodes are
driven by CREDIT data only, never by the AI Capital score, and
'TRANSMISSION CONFIRMED' requires evidence from the credit nodes
themselves.
Spread levels are percent (5.5 = 550bp); moves are percentage points
over the stated window (0.5 = 50bp).

ai_credit._comment: Not a market spread — the deployers' own borrowing, from their filings. Net debt against operating cash flow, and how fast borrowings are growing.

confirmation._comment: How many CREDIT nodes (ai_credit excluded — it is the issuers, not the market) must be RED before transmission is called confirmed, and AMBER before it is called forming.

_comment: V2 section 9. Nvidia's revenue growth against the deployers' aggregate
capex growth. Both grow together in a working capital cycle; the
signal is the gap. Fractions, so 0.30 = 30 percentage points.
V2 section 11. Hunter x AI Capital interpretation matrix.
The rule this encodes: elevated AI capital stress with calm credit is
EARLY WATCH, never a confirmed bust. Progression requires credit to
move, not merely for capex to look stretched.
V2 section 14. A quarterly fundamental only counts as a change when the
MODEL moves — a new filing that leaves every reading where it was is
not news, and must not generate a daily entry.

alerts._comment: Section 17. The alerts table PK (date, kind, key) is the dedup mechanism.

_comment: LONG DURATION / TREASURY CONVEXITY. Decision support for a concentrated
long-duration Treasury position (reference: 2056 principal STRIP).
Informed by the Michael Green thesis of 2026-09-29.
THE ONE THING THIS MUST NOT ENCODE is 'recession = buy bonds'. A
recession only helps a 29-year zero if it pulls the LONG REAL yield or
the term premium down. A stagflationary or fiscal-stress recession
leaves long yields where they are or pushes them higher, and the holder
loses badly because duration cuts both ways. That distinction is
structural here, not editorial: the macro pillar is MULTIPLIED by an
inflation-compatibility factor, so growth deterioration alongside
accelerating inflation contributes nothing at all rather than
contributing a little.
BANDS ARE PERCENTILES OF EACH SERIES' OWN HISTORY wherever the history
supports it, per the brief, rather than absolute yield levels that
would silently encode a view about the right level of rates. The two
exceptions are documented at the fields that use them.
HISTORY LIMITS, which bound what the percentiles mean:
DGS30        1980-       46y  (continuous, incl. the 2002-06 suspension)
THREEFYTP10  1990-       36y
DFII30       2010-02-22- 16y  <- 30Y TIPS were not issued 2001-2010
DLTIIT       2000-       26y  backtest only, 10y+ AVERAGE maturity
A 96th percentile on DFII30 is a 96th percentile of sixteen years. The
UI says so; do not quietly upgrade it to 'since 1980'.

weights._comment: Pillar caps, summing to 5.0. 40/35/25 per the brief.

valuation._comment: Percentile bands. Higher yield = cheaper duration = higher score.

_comment: Consumes the existing cards' OUTPUTS. No recession model is rebuilt
here and no new growth series is fetched.
The veto layer. Answers one question: could the Fed and the long end
plausibly respond to weaker growth with lower rates?
core_hot_pct is an ABSOLUTE 3% annualised rather than a percentile.
Core CPI's own distribution since 1980 includes the disinflation of
the early eighties, so its percentiles are dominated by a regime that
will not recur; 3% is the level at which the long end stops being able
to rally on growth weakness, which is the actual question.
STAGFLATION VETO. Counts conditions; 0 OFF, 1 WATCH, 2+ ACTIVE.
ACTIVE caps the total at the WATCH band. WATCH caps it below 4.5 so a
recession signal alone can never read EXCEPTIONAL, which is the
specific outcome the brief forbids.
SETUP vs CONFIRMATION, kept apart on purpose. A 5.0 setup that is NOT
CONFIRMED means yields look historically cheap and are still rising.
Five tests; 0-1 Not confirmed, 2-3 Partial, 4-5 Confirmed.
WHAT IS DRIVING THE LONG-END? Splits the 30Y nominal move into its
real and breakeven legs over 20 and 60 trading days.
We CANNOT observe Green's passive-flow mechanism in yield data, so the
vocabulary stops at what the decomposition actually supports:
'Consistent with a non-inflation / term-premium driven sell-off'.
Never 'passive selling' or 'mechanical selling' from these inputs.

bands._comment: Brief section 1. Vocabulary only — no BUY/SELL anywhere.

confidence._comment: Below low_coverage the score is withheld as LOW DATA CONFIDENCE rather than presented as complete.
